scenes.purpose: To introduce the lesson topic – the Water Cycle.
scenes.teacher_script: Hello, young geographers! Today, we're going to explore the incredible journey of water on our planet, known as the Water Cycle. This vital process keeps water moving, sustaining life everywhere!

scenes.purpose: To define the key terms necessary for understanding the Water Cycle.
scenes.teacher_script: Before we trace water's path, let's quickly understand three important terms: Evaporation, Condensation, and Precipitation. These are the main actions in the water cycle.

template_data.main_concept: Key Terms of the Water Cycle

attributes.name: Evaporation
attributes.description: The process where water changes into invisible water vapour, mainly due to the sun's heat. Maximum evaporation happens from oceans.

attributes.name: Condensation
attributes.description: The process where water vapour in the air cools down and changes back into tiny water droplets. These droplets group together to form clouds.

attributes.name: Precipitation
attributes.description: Any form of water that falls from the clouds to the Earth's surface. This can be rain, snow, hail, or even dew and fog.

scenes.purpose: To explain the complete, cyclical process of the Water Cycle.
scenes.teacher_script: Now, let's put these terms together to understand the full journey! Water continuously moves from the Earth's surface to the atmosphere and back again in a cycle.

template_data.title: The Water Cycle: A Never-Ending Journey
stages: 1. Evaporation: Water from oceans, rivers, and lakes turns into vapour and rises into the atmosphere.
2. Condensation & Cloud Formation: As vapour rises, it cools, turning into tiny water droplets that form clouds.
3. Precipitation: When clouds become heavy, water falls back to Earth as rain, snow, or hail.
4. Collection & Runoff: Water flows over land as streams and rivers, eventually returning to the seas, ready to evaporate again!

scenes.purpose: To test the student's understanding of a key process in the Water Cycle.
scenes.teacher_script: Fantastic! You've learned how water travels around our Earth. Let's see if you can answer this quick question based on what we just discussed.

template_data.question: What is the process called when water vapour cools and changes back into liquid droplets to form clouds?
